scope: Snowmoon chapters 2-4 only. No later reveals.

screens.title: Over a thousand people are watching
screens.instruction: Minpentai is a high-school programming game from Dzego. The biggest matches are played in a giant room inside a mountain shaped like a pyramid.
screens.caption: Players hand over their devices, pass a drone scan, and play at a console wearing display glasses.
screens.imageNote: Image · players at their consoles in display glasses, the crowd rising behind them

claims.text: A high-school programming game, played across Dzego
A giant room inside a pyramid-shaped mountain, over a thousand people
Devices handed over; drone scan; console and display glasses
Countdown: MU GU GEI FA, starting in fifty ticks

spec.board: No board. Image slot for an illustrator reference, with the countdown lettered over it.
spec.pace: The strip counts 50 to 0 ticks on arrival over 2 s. Decorative; never blocks the button.

screens.title: Your last season
screens.instruction: You're a young player in Dzego, in your last year allowed to compete. Win the championship and you go to the nationals.
screens.caption: “This year is the last year I can participate, and if I win, go to the nationals.” Zei Leimin, a player in the book.

ladder.label: QUARTER-FINAL
ladder.note: Lose here and you “have to find another career. Or try harder for next year!”

screens.rival: IN THE DRAW: A RIVAL WHO HAS BEATEN YOU 3 OF 3

claims.text: Last year to participate; winning leads to the nationals
Prize money (for a compute box, in Zei's case)
Losing a quarter-final: find another career, or try harder next year
A rival who had beaten him three out of three times

spec.board: No board. Season ladder drawn in the board slot.
spec.pace: Ladder rows fade in top to bottom, 80 ms apart.

screens.title: The board moves on its own
screens.instruction: Once a match starts, the cells move by themselves. Press play and watch.
screens.caption: The board updates in 2×2 blocks, and the blocks shift by one cell every turn.

claims.text: The battle unfolds by itself between intervention turns
2×2 blocks on a grid that shifts each turn, recovered from the chapter 4 figure

spec.board: Scripted: 6 lone cells and 2 gliders on the 48 × 32 board, 1×. Fixed grid; only cells move.
spec.idle: Plays 16 turns, then the button reads NEXT.
spec.detects: Turn 16 reached, however it got there.

screens.title: “Rotate one eighty if three”
screens.instruction: That is the book's name for the rule. Cells only move inside their 2×2 block, so none are ever created or destroyed.
screens.caption: Zoomed in on one cell: it hops to the opposite corner of its block every turn, and is back where it started after four turns.

claims.text: The rule's name
Recovered exactly from the animated figure
Live cells never created or destroyed; lone-cell hop

spec.board: One lone cell, 3×, its current block outlined and the opposite corner marked.
spec.idle: Steps 4 turns; the block outline follows the shifting grid.

screens.title: Time runs both ways
screens.instruction: Step back and you get the true past, not a guess. That is why any wall that can be built can also be destroyed.
screens.caption: Outlines show where the glider was at turns 0 and 4.

claims.text: Any wall that can be created in some way can be destroyed in some way
Every step can be undone exactly

spec.board: One glider. Arrives at turn 8 with outlines at its turn-0 and turn-4 positions. 2×.
spec.idle: Steps back to turn 0, then forward to turn 8 again.
spec.detects: A step back taken by the visitor.

screens.title: Build a glider
screens.instruction: Tap the four outlined squares. Your glider will travel two cells every four turns.
screens.caption: Placed one cell off, the same shape stays put. The outline marks a working position.
screens.captionOff: That shape is one cell off, so it stays put.

claims.text: Gliders fly out and do the work
The 4-cell shape, 2 cells per 4 turns, one cell off doesn't travel

spec.board: Empty, 3×, four ghost squares at a working position.
spec.visitor: Tap to place or remove cells. A tap anywhere in the ghost area fills the nearest empty ghost square, because cells are 24 px at 3×.
spec.idle: Fills the remaining ghost squares 250 ms apart, then plays 8 turns.
spec.detects: Engine glider detection, with direction. Built off-position: caption shows captionOff and the ghost stays lit.

screens.title: Rocks bounce gliders
screens.instruction: Grey rocks never move. A glider that hits one bounces off, like light off a mirror.
screens.caption: The book has rock formations, and walls that reflect gliders. These rocks are the sandbox's own.

claims.text: Rock formations on the board
Walls reflect gliders
Fixed rock cells that bounce gliders like mirrors

spec.board: Preset: a glider striking a rock. 2×.
spec.visitor: Play, step, add or remove rocks.
spec.idle: Plays until a bounce is detected, then 8 more turns.
spec.pace: 6 turns/s, 400 ms hold on the bounce turn.

screens.title: Your symbol
screens.instruction: A copy of your symbol lets you see everything within thirty squares of it. Here a glider forms one by striking a pair of rocks at just the right angle.
screens.caption: Framed means recognised. It holds for one turn, then the glider's pieces fly apart.

claims.text: A copy of your symbol lets you see everything within thirty squares
Spaceships crash into rocks and leave copies of a symbol behind
The 4-cell symbol shape, and forming it with one glider and two rocks

spec.board: A glider and a rock arranged so the strike forms the symbol. 2×.
spec.visitor: Play, step back to the symbol turn.
spec.idle: Plays until a symbol is recognised, holds that turn for 1.5 s, then plays 6 more turns.

screens.title: Lose them all and you're out
screens.instruction: A glider fired into a symbol destroys it for good. When every copy of a player's symbol is gone, that player is eliminated.
screens.caption: Drawn alone, a symbol stays in place but cycles through 12 arrangements. All of them are recognised.

claims.text: Every one of a player's symbols destroyed: that player is out
A glider destroys a symbol for good; 12 arrangements

spec.board: A lone symbol, framed, with a glider lined up to hit it. 2×.
spec.idle: Plays until SYMBOLS reads 0, holds 600 ms.

screens.title: A real match
screens.instruction: This is an illustration of a full match. The sandbox can't play one yet.

claims.text: See the six frame captions

spec.board: Scripted six-frame illustration on a 96 × 64 board in owner colours. Frames 1–5 show your team's view with fog; frame 6 is the audience view.
spec.visitor: Tap a frame number to jump to it.
spec.idle: Plays all six frames, then NEXT.
spec.pace: 1.8 s per frame, 300 ms crossfade, fog edge eases outward.

screens.title: Why it's hard
screens.instruction: Five things every player is up against.

reasons.text: You see only what is near your symbols.
You act only in short intervention turns. In between, your plan runs without you.
Priests pick a new rule for every match, and you learn it only at the start.
The rules run backward exactly, so no wall is invincible.
Teams can be random, and your teammate might be your rival.

claims.text: Limited vision
Intervention turns only
A new rule every game, set by priests, learned at the start
No invincible wall
Random 2 v 2 teams; cooperating with a rival

spec.board: Illustration: match frame 2 in a player's fogged view.

screens.title: The book's own board
screens.instruction: This is the opening frame of the board shown in chapter 4. Play it, then make your own.
screens.caption: The book's figure is cropped. The right half was reconstructed so the visible half replays its 120 frames exactly.

claims.text: The animated board figure
Right half reconstructed to match 120 frames

spec.board: Preset: the book's board, 1×, playing on arrival.
spec.idle: Enters free play with this board loaded and marks the tutorial as seen.

frames.title: Setup
frames.caption: The board starts black. Each player tests designs in a private sandbox, then places symbols and first structures in their home corner.

frames.title: Spreading
frames.caption: Gliders fly out and hit rocks. Spaceships crash on purpose and leave copies of your symbol, so you see more of the board.

frames.title: Intervention turn
frames.caption: Every so often, everyone may put down new squares near any copy of their symbol. Then the plan runs without you.

frames.title: Clash
frames.caption: Stray gliders wreck factories and walls reflect them. A stream of gliders forms your symbol inside enemy ground for exactly one turn.

frames.title: A player out
frames.caption: Every copy of one rival's symbol has been destroyed, so that rival is out.

frames.title: Endgame
frames.caption: Most of the field is now a high-entropy wasteland. The audience sees all of it; players never do.
